sets.title: Festival Talk Schedule
sets.contentHtml:
A literature festival schedules six talks, one on each day from Monday to Saturday of a single week. The six speakers are Farah, Gopal, Hema, Imran, Jaya and Kunal, and each gives exactly one talk. Every talk is held in one of three halls: Lotus, Maple and Neem. Each hall hosts exactly two of the six talks, and no hall is used on two consecutive days.

The following is also known:

  1. Jaya speaks in Neem.
  2. Hema speaks in Maple.
  3. Gopal speaks on the day immediately before the day of Hema's talk.
  4. Farah and Imran speak in the same hall.
  5. Exactly two days separate the talks of Farah and Kunal (for example, if one of them speaks on Monday, the other speaks on Thursday).
  6. Imran speaks on a later day than Jaya.

sets.title: Five-Team Hockey League
sets.contentHtml:
Five hockey teams, P, Q, R, S and T, played a single round-robin tournament, in which each team played every other team exactly once. A win earned 3 points, a draw earned 1 point to each team, and a loss earned 0 points.

The following facts are known about the tournament:

  1. No two teams finished with the same number of points.
  2. Exactly three matches ended in a draw.
  3. R was the only team that did not lose any match.
  4. T did not win any match.
  5. Q won more matches than any other team.
  6. P finished with exactly 7 points.

sets.title: Archery Scorecard
sets.contentHtml:
Four archers, Aditi, Bhavna, Charu and Divya, each shot exactly four arrows at a target. Each arrow either landed in one of four rings or missed the target, and scored points as follows: Gold 10, Red 7, Blue 4, Black 1, Miss 0. An archer's score is the total of the points of her four arrows.

RingGoldRedBlueBlackMiss
Points107410

The following is known:

  1. The four archers' scores were 31, 25, 22 and 15, in some order.
  2. Altogether, exactly four arrows hit Gold and exactly one arrow missed the target.
  3. Bhavna did not hit Gold with any arrow.
  4. Aditi scored more than Charu.
  5. Every archer hit Blue with at least one arrow.
  6. Divya hit Black with exactly one arrow, and Charu hit Black with at least one arrow.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following speakers can NOT give the talk on Monday?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. Each hall hosts exactly two talks. Farah and Imran share a hall. If that hall were Neem, Neem would host Farah, Imran and Jaya (three talks); if it were Maple, Maple would host Farah, Imran and Hema. Both are impossible, so Farah and Imran are in Lotus, which is then full. Gopal and Kunal therefore occupy the remaining Neem and Maple slots. Gopal speaks on the day just before Hema (Maple), and Maple cannot be used on consecutive days, so Gopal is in Neem and Kunal is in Maple.

So the hall pairs are Lotus: Farah, Imran; Neem: Jaya, Gopal; Maple: Hema, Kunal, and the two talks of a pair can never be on consecutive days.

Placing the Gopal-Hema block (days numbered 1 = Monday to 6 = Saturday):

  • G-H on 1-2: Farah and Kunal must be 3 apart among days 3-6, so they take 3 and 6; Kunal on 3 would follow Hema (both Maple), so Kunal = 6, Farah = 3. Jaya and Imran take 4 and 5 with Jaya first. Valid: G H F J I K.
  • G-H on 2-3: Farah/Kunal take 1 and 4; Kunal on 4 would follow Hema, so Kunal = 1, Farah = 4; Jaya = 5, Imran = 6. Valid: K G H F J I.
  • G-H on 3-4: Farah/Kunal take 2 and 5; Kunal = 5 is next to Hema, so Kunal = 2, Farah = 5; then Jaya = 1, Imran = 6, making Farah and Imran (both Lotus) consecutive. Invalid.
  • G-H on 4-5: Farah/Kunal take 3 and 6; Kunal = 6 is next to Hema, so Kunal = 3, Farah = 6; Jaya = 1, Imran = 2. Valid: J I K G H F.
  • G-H on 5-6: Farah/Kunal take 1 and 4; Jaya = 2, Imran = 3. Farah = 4 would be next to Imran (Lotus), so Farah = 1, Kunal = 4. Valid: F J I K G H.

Exactly four schedules survive:

ScheduleMonTueWedThuFriSat
1Gopal (Neem)Hema (Maple)Farah (Lotus)Jaya (Neem)Imran (Lotus)Kunal (Maple)
2Kunal (Maple)Gopal (Neem)Hema (Maple)Farah (Lotus)Jaya (Neem)Imran (Lotus)
3Jaya (Neem)Imran (Lotus)Kunal (Maple)Gopal (Neem)Hema (Maple)Farah (Lotus)
4Farah (Lotus)Jaya (Neem)Imran (Lotus)Kunal (Maple)Gopal (Neem)Hema (Maple)

Monday is taken by Gopal, Kunal, Jaya or Farah in the four schedules. Hema always speaks the day after Gopal, so Hema can never be on Monday. Answer: Hema.

questions.stemHtml: How many points did Q score in the tournament?
questions.solutionHtml:
Deductions. P has 7 points from 4 matches. With w wins and d draws, 3w + d = 7 and w + d ≤ 4, so w = 2, d = 1: P won 2, drew 1, lost 1.

Q won more matches than anyone, so Q has at least 3 wins (P already has 2). R never lost, so Q did not beat R; hence Q beat P, S and T. Q must have lost a match (R is the only unbeaten team), and its only remaining match is against R: R beat Q. Q has 3 wins and 1 loss = 9 points.

P's only loss is to Q. P could not beat R (unbeaten), so P drew with R and beat S and T.

Six results are now fixed (Q beat P, S, T; R beat Q; P drew R; P beat S, T), with one draw (P-R). The remaining matches R-S, R-T and S-T must contain exactly two draws. R cannot lose and T cannot win, so the one decisive match is R beats S, R beats T, or S beats T:

  • R beats S; R-T and S-T drawn: P 7, Q 9, R 8, S 1, T 2.
  • R beats T; R-S and S-T drawn: P 7, Q 9, R 8, S 2, T 1.
  • S beats T; R-S and R-T drawn: P 7, Q 9, R 6, S 4, T 1.

In each case all point totals are distinct and Q has strictly the most wins (R has at most 2), so all three cases are valid.

Q scored 9 points.

questions.stemHtml: What was Aditi's score?
questions.solutionHtml:
